root_cause.text: xfrm_policy_bysel_ctx() kept a pointer to an inexact policy bin and pruned it after releasing net->xfrm.xfrm_policy_lock, allowing concurrent xfrm_hash_rebuild()/__xfrm_policy_inexact_flush() to free that bin and cause a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and diff show the race where CPU0 saves bin from xfrm_policy_inexact_lookup(), unlocks, and later calls xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(bin), while CPU1 under the same lock runs __xfrm_policy_inexact_flush() and kfree_rcu(bin); the fix moves pruning into the locked section by calling __xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(bin, false) before spin_unlock_bh().

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant locked wrapper around inexact policy bin pruning to consolidate pruning calls around the internal helper.
intent_record.what: The change removes the entire static wrapper function `xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(struct xfrm_pol_inexact_bin *b)`, which previously retrieved `struct net *net` from `b->k.net`, acquired `net->xfrm.xfrm_policy_lock` with `spin_lock_bh`, called `__xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(b, false)`, and then released the lock with `spin_unlock_bh`.
intent_record.how: This eliminates a helper that performed locked invocation of the internal prune routine; runtime behavior only changes if call sites are updated elsewhere to invoke the internal function directly or handle locking differently, so this hunk itself indicates consolidation/removal of an indirection rather than a standalone behavioral change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inexact xfrm policy bin pruning during deletion by performing it under the policy lock with the internal prune helper.
intent_record.what: The call to prune an inexact policy bin during delete operations was moved from after `spin_unlock_bh(&net->xfrm.xfrm_policy_lock)` to before the unlock, and the function call was changed from `xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(bin)` to `__xfrm_policy_inexact_prune_bin(bin, false)`.
intent_record.how: This makes bin pruning happen while the xfrm policy lock is still held, using the internal prune helper with an explicit boolean argument. At runtime, it prevents the inexact policy bin from being modified after releasing the lock, reducing the risk of races or inconsistent state during policy deletion.

relevance_review.reason: The change is directly about inexact policy bin pruning, which is the operation involved in the use-after-free root cause. Removing/consolidating the pruning wrapper affects how pruning is invoked around locking, so it is tied to the vulnerable code path rather than being unrelated refactoring.

The change directly addresses the root cause: it moves inexact policy bin pruning to occur under the xfrm policy lock via the internal prune helper, preventing the unlocked pruning/use-after-free race with concurrent rebuild/flush operations.

candidates.rationale: This prunes the saved inexact bin after the caller has already released xfrm_policy_lock, matching the root cause of using a bin pointer outside the lock where concurrent rebuild/flush can free it.
The lock is dropped before pruning the remembered bin, creating the race window in which another thread can rebuild/flush and free the bin before it is pruned.
This dereferences the bin pointer inside the pruning wrapper; if the bin was freed after the caller released the policy lock, this becomes a use-after-free trigger.

vuln_statements.explanation: This prunes a previously saved inexact policy bin after the caller has released xfrm_policy_lock. Because the bin pointer is retained and used outside the lock, concurrent xfrm_hash_rebuild()/__xfrm_policy_inexact_flush() can free that bin first, leading to a use-after-free.

Releasing xfrm_policy_lock before pruning the remembered inexact bin creates the race window described in the root cause. After this unlock, another thread can rebuild or flush the inexact policy structures and free the bin before the later prune call uses it.

This dereferences the bin pointer inside the pruning wrapper. If the bin was freed after the policy lock was dropped and before pruning occurred, this statement becomes part of the use-after-free manifestation.
